input.question: Why is gold worth more than silver?
input.ground_truth: Originally, because Gold was rarer, therefore harder to get hold of: the standard rule of supply and demand means that a rarer metal, where both are in demand, will be more expensive. Nowadays, silver is actually rarer, but the perception has been, for hundreds of years, that gold is rarer and more expensive... so there's a higher demand for gold. That means that although gold has greater supply than silver, the demand for gold is still significantly higher: enough that the price stays higher. **If you have 10 pieces of silver, and 20 pieces of gold, but 10 people want the silver and 30 people want the gold... which will you get a higher price for?**
